What exactly do RecapGenerated, RecapRefused and RecapFailed carry? Blocks every CU5 mark. Recommended (a): the proposal in contracts/cu5-generate-recap.md (RecapGenerated: bookId,tier,position,content,words,bands,stripped,ending,text sealed,audioSeconds,voice,generatedAt; RecapRefused: +kind,reason,preparedThrough?,inChapter?; RecapFailed: +step,cause). Alternative (b): the model's strings only, no kind/step.

Where do the recap text and its window live (D17 reads them from the log; Principle IX; D11/D83 erase on removal)? Recommended (a): text sealed in the event with ForgettableWords, window by reference (position+content), audio in a store deleted with the book. Alternatives: (b) text and window both sealed in the event; (c) both behind a store, event holds a reference and digest.

What does the stream say when a request is served from the cache? Recommended (a): nothing appended (a second RecapGenerated would reopen CU7's hearing and reset CU8's thumb); CU4's fold leaving a re-asked cached key at 'standing' is the follow-up. Alternative (b): a new event RecapServed.

Who re-speaks a recap when the voice changed (D3, FR-034) and is it recorded? Recommended (a): CU5 re-speaks on the next request at a generated key whose audio is not in the current voice; audio kept per recap+voice; no event. Alternatives: (b) a further RecapGenerated (reopens hearing, resets rating); (c) CU6 re-speaks at play time.

Which text covers a position (FR-009, FR-021)? Recommended (a): coverage is the transcript's; EPUB text replaces words only in chapters before the position's chapter, the transcript is the window inside the position's chapter. Alternatives: (b) EPUB text inside the position's chapter too (needs sentence alignment); (c) aligned text alone may cover.

Is a word inside the window by the second or the minute (FR-002/FR-028 vs FR-031/A5)? Recommended (a): the window ends at the last word ended at or before the position's second; FR-031 is a floor on coarseness. Alternative (b): floor of the position's minute.

What does the writer enforce about a draft's length and gradient, and where do bands begin and end (D12 is silent on out-of-tolerance drafts, straddling sentences, windows under 10 minutes; FR-005 vs the drawn 'Recent - Chapters 12 to 13')? Recommended (a): tell the drafter, attribute and record, enforce nothing; straddling goes to the more recent band; Recent = current + previous chapter. Alternatives: (b) fail a draft outside +-15%; (c) one bounded redraft.
Is a position of 59 or 60 seconds inside 'the first minute'? Recommended (a): under 60 seconds is refused, 60 and over is not. Alternative (b): 60 and under.

What is a recap at a position past the end of the book (CU4 accepts any non-negative position)? Recommended (a): refuse with a fifth reason (past the end of the book). Alternative (b): treat as the end, key keeps the position asked.

Does the writer skip a request whose book was removed? Recommended (a): add BookRemoved to CU5's reads in the model and skip/close such requests. Alternative (b): no model change, draft anyway (PR1's D99 reading), which would repopulate an erased stream.
Is the voice picker's play-sample button (D25) part of CU5? Recommended (a): no, a task of CU6 and named in the split's Defers column. Alternative (b): yes here, as a route and a task.

Which drafting/checking/speech providers are bound, and what do adapters do until a person names them (a vendor SDK is a package-manifest change no slice may make)? Recommended (a): ports with a deterministic in-process adapter in the composition root; a real adapter once a person names the provider and supplies credentials. Alternative (b): real adapter in this slice.

If the second pass strips the ending sentence (FR-004 vs FR-007), what is spoken? Recommended (a): D5's rule, survivors are spoken and ending is the last sentence actually spoken. Alternatives: (b) refuse as nothing-survived; (c) append a deterministic position sentence no model wrote.
